q: Which term describes work on a building that changes materials, partitions, opening locations/sizes, structural parts, or existing utilities/equipment, but does not add to the building's total floor area?
n: Alteration changes materials, partitions, openings, structure or services without adding floor area; an addition adds area and a renovation improves value or looks.

q: What is the term for relocating a building or part of it from its original site to another spot, whether on the same lot or a different one?
n: Moving is relocating a building, wholly or in part, to another spot on the same or another lot.

q: Which term refers to any physical alteration to a building or structure meant to raise its value or usefulness, or to enhance its appearance?
n: Renovation is any physical change that raises value or usefulness or improves appearance.

q: According to Rule II of the IRR of PD 1096, which of these statements about the building official does NOT hold true?
o: The building official must either be a duly registered architect or civil engineer
The building official must be of good moral character
The building official must have at least five years of diversified and professional experience in building design and construction
All of the above are true
n: A Building Official must be a registered architect or civil engineer of good moral character with at least five years of building design and construction experience, so none of the statements is false.

q: Under Rule II of the IRR of the National Building Code, which of these violations carries the heaviest penalty?
o: Use or occupancy of building/structure without appropriate Certificate of Occupancy
Non-compliance with the work stoppage order for the alteration, addition, conversion, or repair without permit
Failure to post Certificate of Occupancy
Non-compliance with work stoppage order for construction or demolition without permit
n: Ignoring a stop-work order on construction or demolition done without a permit is the gravest offense in the schedule of fines, above occupancy without a certificate.
ref: IRR of PD 1096, Rule II — Administrative fines

q: Who has the responsibility of declaring a building ruinous or dangerous?
o: This is the building official’s duty
n: The Building Official, not the architect or the PRBOA, declares buildings dangerous or ruinous and orders their repair or demolition.

q: Which of the following structures is exempt from needing a building permit?
o: A mini-aviary measuring 3 meters x 4 meters with a maximum height of less than 6 meters measured from the ground to the apex of the roof
A greenhouse that measures 2 meters x 3 meters only
A small patio, only 25 sqm. in area, resting directly on the ground
A low garden masonry wall that is only 6 meters long and only 1.5 meters high
n: Greenhouses, sheds and aviaries up to 6.00 sqm need no permit; a 12 sqm aviary, a 25 sqm patio (limit 20 sqm) and a 1.50 m garden wall (limit 1.20 m) all do.

q: What is the required minimum clearance between a building's eaves and its rear or side property lines?
o: None of the above. Setbacks are measured not to the eaves, but to the exterior faces of the walls.
n: Eaves, canopies and awnings over required windows must stay at least 750 mm from the side and rear property lines.

q: For an industrial building fronting a 30-meter-wide road right-of-way, what front setback distance is the minimum required?
n: Industrial buildings on a road right-of-way of 30 m or more need at least an 8.00 m front setback, the largest in the IRR setback schedule.
ref: IRR of PD 1096, Rule VIII — setback table

q: What do we call the written authorization from the Building Official permitting an applicant to begin construction once plans and other documents are found compliant with the Code?
n: A building permit is the Building Official's written authority to start work once the plans comply; the FSEC and FSIC are fire-safety documents.

q: Under Rule II of the NBC IRR, which of these are civil/structural documents?
n: Structural plans, roof framing, boring and load tests and seismic analysis all belong to the civil/structural documents, so none is excluded.

q: Firewalls aren't permitted for R1 developments, though an abutment as high as 3.20m may be built if, above a certain height, it is constructed of perforated concrete blocks. What is that height threshold?
n: An R-1 abutment may rise to 3.20 m, but the part above 1.50 m must be perforated or decorative concrete block.

q: Is the owner permitted to start ground preparation and excavation before the building permit itself is issued?
o: No. The owner must wait for the building permit to be issued before he can proceed with excavation works.
Yes, as long as the Building Official issues the Ground Preparation and Excavation Permit and as long as the owner follows the corresponding rules/requirements.
The NBC is silent on this matter.
n: The Building Official may issue a ground preparation and excavation permit ahead of the building permit.

q: May an owner occupy finished portions of a building while construction continues on other parts?
o: No. The entire building must be completed first and the Certificate of Occupancy for the entire building must be issued before anyone can occupy any portion of the building.
No, this is extremely dangerous. There must be no ongoing works within the building before anyone may be allowed to occupy it.
Yes, if the Building Official grants a Partial Certificate of Occupancy to the owner.
n: A partial Certificate of Occupancy lets the owner use finished portions while work continues elsewhere.

q: On a sloping lot where the highest and lowest points differ by 2.00m in elevation, which point is used as the established grade line when determining building height?
o: The lowest point of the lot
The highest point of the lot
The average between the two points
n: When the footprint edges differ by less than 3.00 m in elevation, the highest adjoining grade is the established grade; above 3.00 m the average is used.
ref: IRR of PD 1096, Rule VII — building height

q: What minimum parking slot size must be provided for a standard truck?
n: A standard truck bay is 3.60 × 12.00 m; articulated trucks need 3.60 × 18.00 m and cars 2.50 × 5.00 m.
ref: IRR of PD 1096, Rule VII — parking slot table

q: What do you obtain when you add together the ISA and the USA?
n: Total open space within the lot (TOSL) = impervious surface area (ISA) + unpaved surface area (USA).

q: Subtracting the ISAmax from the MACA yields which value?
n: MACA = PSOmax + ISAmax, so MACA − ISAmax = PSOmax, the maximum site occupancy.

q: What result do you get when you multiply the FLAR by the TLA?
n: FLAR × TLA gives the gross floor area (GFA) allowed on the lot.

q: Per the National Building Code, what is the smallest floor area allowed for a habitable room?
n: Rooms for human habitation must be at least 6.00 sqm with a least dimension of 2.00 m.

q: What is the minimum required air space allotment per occupant in a habitable room?
n: Habitable rooms need 14 cu m of air space per occupant; school rooms need 3 cu m and workshops 12 cu m.

q: An interior lot access road serving 4 dwelling units must have what minimum width?
n: An access road serving a small cluster of 4 units may be 3.00 m wide; wider roads are required as the number of units grows.
ref: IRR of PD 1096, Rule VIII — interior lot access

q: What minimum ceiling height applies to the seventh floor of a naturally ventilated building?
n: Naturally ventilated habitable rooms need at least 2.70 m ceilings on every floor; the 2.10 m head-room applies only to upper floors of artificially ventilated buildings.

q: In agricultural zones, the NBC mandates a minimum easement of how much on each side of a waterway?
n: Waterway easements are 3 m in urban areas, 20 m in agricultural areas and 40 m in forest areas on each bank.
ref: Water Code, Art. 51 (cited in the PD 1096 IRR)

q: Townhouse developments typically fall under which zoning classification?
n: Townhouses fall under R-4; R-2 covers duplexes and R-5 high-rise residential.
ref: IRR of PD 1096, Rule VII — zoning classes

q: Per Article 1723 of the Civil Code, whom does the law hold liable when a building collapses more than 10 years after completion due to the use of substandard materials?
o: The architect or the engineer who drew up the plans
The contractor and the construction supervisor
The building official who reviewed and approved the c. plans
n: Collapse from inferior materials or construction within the 15-year period makes the contractor liable, jointly with the architect or engineer who supervised construction.

q: Which document must be secured before a completed building may be used or occupied?
n: No building may be used or occupied until the Building Official issues a Certificate of Occupancy.

q: The Building Code mandates that the owner engage a full-time construction inspector. What license must this inspector hold?
n: PD 1096 Sec. 308 requires the owner to engage a duly licensed architect or civil engineer for full-time inspection and supervision of the construction work.

q: For an R3 development, which firewall placement arrangement(s) are permitted?
o: Allowed only on one side of property
Allowed on both sides of the property
Allowed on one side and the rear
n: R-3 may have firewalls on both sides, or on one side and the rear; R-2 is limited to one side.
ref: IRR of PD 1096, Rule VII — firewalls

q: What term applies to new construction that adds to the height or floor area of an existing building?
n: An addition is new construction that increases the height or floor area of an existing building.

q: Which construction type uses wood framing protected by fire-resistant materials, giving one-hour fire resistance throughout?
n: Type II is wood framing protected by fire-resistive materials, one-hour fire-resistive throughout.

q: The National Building Code's provisions cover all public and private buildings EXCEPT for which of the following?
o: Buildings made of native materials like wood, nipa, and lumber
Projects that only involve non-structural repairs
n: BP 220 socialized and economic housing projects follow their own standards instead of the NBC.

q: Which of these is NOT a valid basis for declaring a building dangerous?
n: Grounds are structural, fire, sanitation and electrical/mechanical hazards; looks are never a ground.

q: In which zone(s) are Type II constructions disallowed?
n: Highly fire restrictive zones admit only Types IV and V; Type II is allowed in the other two zones.

q: On a non-arcaded road right-of-way, how far may a sign project outward at most?
n: Signs may project up to 1.20 m over a non-arcaded road right-of-way.
ref: IRR of PD 1096, Rule XX — signs

q: If a sign is permitted to project past the property line into an arcaded road right-of-way, what minimum vertical clearance must be kept between the road surface and the sign's underside?
n: Signs over an arcaded RROW must clear the road surface by at least 5.00 m.
ref: IRR of PD 1096, Rule XX — signs

q: Glass panels exceeding 3.00m x 3.00m in size must have a minimum thickness of:
n: The Rule XVIII table requires 15 mm glass for panels over 3.00 × 3.00 m.

q: Per the NBC, escalators may not exceed what maximum speed?
n: Escalators may not run faster than 38 m per minute (125 ft/min).
ref: IRR of PD 1096, Rule XII — escalators

q: Per the NBC, what stairway width is required at minimum for buildings with an occupant load between 10 and 50?
n: Stairs serving 10 to 50 occupants must be at least 0.90 m wide; fewer than 10 need 0.75 m and more than 50 need 1.10 m.

q: To protect pedestrians, what must be provided when the distance from the OFB to the inner edge of the sidewalk equals 75% of the building's height?
o: A fence, a canopy, and a safety net
n: When the building face is more than half the building height from the sidewalk, a 2.40 m fence alone protects pedestrians.

q: On roads narrower than 3.60m, every fence or building corner must be truncated to form a chaflan. What is the minimum width required for this chaflan?
n: Corner buildings and solid fences on streets narrower than 3.60 m need a chaflan of at least 4.00 m.

q: Which formula correctly computes building bulk?
n: Building bulk (volume) = allowable footprint (TLA × PSOmax) × building height limit in meters.
ref: IRR of PD 1096, Guidelines on Building Bulk

q: Which of the following is counted as part of the Gross Floor Area (GFA)?
o: Fire escape structures if complying to standards stair measurements of the NBC
Balconies with an area of 5 square meters
Utility areas equivalent to not more than one-third of one floor
Parking areas equivalent to half the area of one floor
n: Balconies are counted in GFA; fire escapes, utility areas up to a third of a floor and parking areas are excluded.
ref: IRR of PD 1096, Rule VII — GFA

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the steepest slope allowed for a PWD ramp?
n: Table A.1.1: 1:20 is the standard; 1:15 is the steepest allowed, for a ramp up to 10.50 m long with landings every 10 m (the 1994 IRR allowed 1:12).

q: For a ramp at the steepest allowed slope (1:15), a landing is required every 10.00 meters of run under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344. What is the minimum landing length?
n: Sec. A.1.2(d) and Table A.1.1: 1:15 ramps need landings every 10 m, each at least 1800 mm long.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, how wide must a dropped sidewalk at a pedestrian crossing be?
n: Sec. C dropped sidewalks: the width corresponds to the width of the crossing. The 1994 IRR used a fixed 0.90 m curb cut-out.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what minimum size must walkway turnabout spaces have, and how far apart may they be?
o: Minimum dimension of 1.80m, at most 12.00m apart
Minimum dimension of 1.50m, at most 13.50m apart
Minimum dimension of 1.20m, at most 15.00m apart
Minimum dimension of 1.50m, at most 12.00m apart
n: Sec. B.3.7 and C.5.2: turnabout spaces are at least 1800 mm and at most 12.00 m apart (the 1994 IRR used 1.50 m).

q: Handrails required at ramps, stairs, and dropped curbs for crossings must be installed at what height(s)?
n: Handrails on ramps and stairs go at 700 mm and 900 mm, the lower one for children and wheelchair users.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the minimum required width for an accessible parking slot?
n: Sec. A.6.7: accessible parking slots are at least 4.00 m wide by 5.00 m long (the 1994 IRR required 3.70 m).

q: What must be provided at both the top and bottom of a ramp?
o: A curb with a minimum height of 100mm
A level area not less than 1.80m in length
A turnabout space with a minimum dimension of 1.50m
A vestibule with a level space at least 1.50m wide and 2.00m deep
n: Every ramp needs a level landing at least 1.80 m long at the top and bottom.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what are the minimum dimensions of an accessible toilet cubicle?
n: Sec. C.6.3(a): accessible toilet cubicles are at least 1800 × 1800 mm (the 1994 IRR required 1.70 × 1.80 m).

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the minimum clear size of an accessible elevator car?
n: Sec. C.8.5: at least 1,200 mm wide by 1,400 mm deep with a 900 mm door (transport terminals need 1,400 × 1,500 mm). The 1994 IRR allowed 1.10 × 1.40 m.

q: What is the farthest an accessible elevator may be located from the entrance?
n: Accessible elevators must be no more than 30 m from the entrance and easy to find by signs.

q: For PWD washrooms, what is the tallest a lavatory counter may be?
n: Accessible lavatories are mounted 800 mm from the floor with at least 650 mm leg room below.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what minimum clear width must doors have?
n: Sec. C.2.1: all doors have a clear width of at least 900 mm (the 1994 IRR required 800 mm).

q: A central refuge area at least 1.50m deep is required at crossings when the road being crossed is wider than:
n: Roads wider than 10.00 m need a central refuge island at least 1.50 m deep at crossings.

q: Fires involving live/energized electrical equipment fall under which fire classification?
n: Class C fires involve energized electrical equipment; water must not be used until the power is cut.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the maximum cross gradient of a dropped sidewalk toward the road?
n: Dropped sidewalks slope toward the road at no more than 1:100 so water does not collect; the level area may sit at most 19 mm above the gutter.

q: Which standpipe system type has pipes that stay dry under normal conditions, with water only entering through fire service connections when needed?
n: A dry standpipe holds no water until the fire service pumps it in through the connection.

q: BP 220 sets what maximum riser height for stairs?
n: BP 220 limits stair risers to 0.25 m.

q: What is the smallest allowable stair tread width under BP 220?
n: BP 220 treads must be at least 0.20 m.

q: Fires fueled by ordinary combustibles like wood, cloth, rubber, and plastics are classified as:
n: Class A fires burn ordinary combustibles like wood, paper, cloth, rubber and many plastics.

q: Which of these arrangements is disallowed under both BP 220 and PD 957?
o: A 500 m block with a 2 m mid-block alley
A 400 m block with a 2 m mid-block alley
n: No block may exceed 400 m, alley or not; the alley is needed only once a block passes 250 m.

q: What term describes any visual or audible signal from a device or system meant to alert building occupants or firefighters to a fire hazard?
n: A fire alarm is any audible or visual signal that warns occupants or firefighters of fire.

q: What is the term for an integrated network of hydraulically designed piping, fitted with outlets in a systematic pattern, that automatically releases water when triggered by heat or fire combustion products?
n: A sprinkler system is a hydraulically designed network of pipes and heads that discharges water automatically when heated.

q: PD 957 prescribes what ratio between saleable and non-saleable lots?
n: PD 957 caps saleable area at 70%, leaving at least 30% for roads, parks and facilities; BP 220 sets no fixed ratio.

q: Which statement below is accurate?
o: An alley must have a minimum width of 1.20 m.
An alley may be used as property access for socialized developments only
A pathwalk length of up to 60.00 m. is allowed
A pathwalk may be used as property access for socialized and economic developments
n: Pathwalks are 3.0 m wide and at most 60 m long; alleys (2.0 m) may not serve as lot access.

q: Excluding mezzanines, what minimum ceiling height applies to socialized and economic housing?
n: BP 220 habitable rooms need at least a 2.00 m ceiling (1.80 m above and below a mezzanine).

q: Where should results of the annual fire pump flow test, annual main drain test, and standpipe water flow test be recorded?
n: Annual fire pump, main drain and standpipe flow tests are logged in the Fire Safety Maintenance Report (FSMR).

q: BP 220 specifies what acceptable range of handrail heights?
n: BP 220 handrails are 0.80 to 1.20 m above the tread.

q: For economic housing, single-detached units require a minimum lot area of:
n: Economic housing single-detached lots need at least 72 sqm; socialized ones 64 sqm.

q: Single-detached socialized housing units must have what minimum lot frontage?
n: Socialized single-detached lots need an 8 m frontage.

q: Socialized and economic housing must observe what minimum side setback?
n: BP 220 side yards are 1.5 m, front setbacks 1.5 m and rear yards 2.0 m.

q: Fires involving combustible cooking media such as vegetable or animal oils and fats in cooking appliances are classified as:
n: Class K fires involve cooking oils and fats, which need wet-chemical extinguishers.

q: BP 220 lists minimum basic needs for human settlements. Which three appear last on that list?
o: Storm drainage, parks and playgrounds, power
Solid and liquid waste disposal, parks and playgrounds, power
n: The list runs water, circulation, storm drainage, waste disposal, parks and playgrounds, and power last.

q: Medium-cost and open-market housing developments with a density of 20 lots or dwelling units per hectare or less must set aside what minimum percentage of gross area for parks and playgrounds?
n: Low-density projects (20 or fewer lots per hectare) give 3.5% of the gross area to parks; high density gives 9%.

q: Open-market housing units must have a minimum floor area of:
n: PD 957 open market housing needs 42 sqm of floor area; medium cost needs 30 sqm.

q: PD 957 requires units to be delivered at what minimum level of completion?
o: Shell house with doors and windows
n: PD 957 requires a complete house; shell houses are allowed only for socialized housing.

q: What is the minimum lot area needed for open-market duplex housing?
n: Open market duplex lots need 96 sqm; medium cost duplexes need 80 sqm.

q: Under BP 220, what is the minimum firewall thickness?
n: BP 220 firewalls are at least 150 mm (6 in) thick and rise 0.30 m above the roof.

q: Subdivisions fronting main public roads must reserve setbacks on either side of the entrance for public utility vehicles. What are the minimum required dimensions?
n: Entrances on main roads need 3.0 × 5.0 m setbacks on both sides for PUVs to stop.

q: Per PD 957, what minimum floor area applies to a medium-cost family condominium unit?
n: Medium cost family condominium units need 22 sqm; open market ones 36 sqm.

q: What term describes an integrated piping system linked to an extinguishing agent source that suppresses fire once triggered by its automatic detection device?
n: An automatic fire suppression system is piping tied to an agent supply that discharges when its detector trips.

q: What term refers to the maximum number of people permitted to occupy a given building or space?
n: Occupant load is the maximum number of people a building or space may hold.

q: Which document is issued once it's determined that a design and its specifications comply with the Fire Code?
n: The Fire Safety Evaluation Clearance (FSEC) is issued when the plans comply with the Fire Code; the FSIC comes after inspection.

q: Which architect's conduct violates the Code of Ethics?
o: An architect who credits half of his commission from the supplier to the owner’s bill (to add to the owner’s discount)
An architect who recommends the method of arbitration when it comes to settling disputes
An architect who refuses to make schematic sketches without payment for a client who is short of money
An architect who informs his colleague that he is being hired by the latter’s former client as a new architect for a project
n: Crediting a supplier's commission to the owner still means the architect took a secret commission, which the Code forbids.

q: Under what condition may an architect accept a gift from a supplier?
o: The architect is never allowed to accept gifts, no matter how small
Only when the gift will not cloud the architect’s judgment and objectivity
Only when the gift was solicited by the architect
Only when the gift does not exceed the contract amount awarded to that supplier
n: A modest gift is acceptable only if it does not sway the architect's judgment; solicited gifts are never allowed.

q: Which architect's conduct does NOT violate the Code of Ethics?
o: An architect who asks to be considered for a project even though the owner has already begun negotiations with another architect (but no contract yet)
An architect who accepts a commission to remodel a building after notifying the original architect of the commission and ensuring that the previous architect’s contract was properly terminated
An architect who fails to pay his draftsmen according to the work contract because of his firm’s financial difficulties
All of these architects are violating the Code of Ethics
n: Taking over a commission is ethical once the earlier architect is notified and the prior contract is properly ended.

q: Between an architect's duty to the client and to the public, which one takes precedence?
o: An architect’s duty to his client
An architect’s duty to the public
n: Duty to the public comes first: an architect may not follow a client into work that endangers public safety.

q: What is the term for an architect, licensed under RA 9266, who bears direct professional responsibility for supervising a project's construction?
n: The architect in charge of construction is the RLA who directly and professionally supervises the construction work.

q: Which of the following does NOT fall within the PRBOA's duties?
o: Administer oaths under the Architecture Act
Run CPD seminars as an automatic CPD provider
Suspend an architect's certificate of registration
Adopt an official seal of the Board
n: The PRBOA administers oaths, suspends registrations and adopts a seal; CPD seminars are run by accredited providers such as the IAPOA, not the Board.

q: Which of these is NOT valid grounds for removing a PRBOA member?
o: Spreading false and malicious rumors about an architect
Dropping a subject from the licensure exam syllabus
Being unable to perform duties because of illness
Manipulating the grades in the licensure exam
n: Board members can be removed for neglect, incompetence, dishonesty or unprofessional conduct; changing the exam syllabus is within the Board's powers.

q: Who among these is disqualified from being elected to the PRBArch today?
o: An architect who has never received a commission for high-rise building projects
An architect who has never been convicted of crimes involving moral turpitude and who has plenty of related experience as current chairman of the Philippine Institute of Architects
An architect who started practicing architecture on September 24, 2003 only
An architect who ceased all teaching functions and connections with any school or review center on September 24, 2010 only
n: A nominee must not be an officer of any professional association at the time of appointment, so a sitting chairman of an architects' group is disqualified.

q: Is a non-Filipino citizen permitted to sit for the architecture licensure examination?
o: No. Only Filipinos are allowed to take the examination.
Yes, if they have experience working under a Filipino mentor for a project on Philippine soil.
Absolutely. The PRC encourages and freely allows all architecture graduates from other countries to take the exam as part of the globalization initiative.
n: Foreigners may take the exam only if their country grants reciprocity to Filipino architects.

q: Which of these constitutes grounds for suspending or revoking an architect's license?
o: Violation of the minor provisions of RA 9266
n: Fraud, unprofessional conduct and violations of the law are all grounds for suspending or revoking a license.

q: Which of these individuals is in violation of RA 9266?
o: An architecture graduate who posts an advertisement on www.OLX.ph that he can prepare plans that are just as good as a licensed architect’s
A secretary who, upon her boss’ instruction, offers her boss’ architectural design services even though her boss is not a licensed architect
A person who uses another name instead of his/her registered name because the new name is more marketable and is easier to remember
All of these persons are violating RA 9266
n: Advertising architectural services while unlicensed, offering them for an unlicensed boss, or practicing under a false name all violate the law.

q: Before a project is actually built, who holds the intellectual property rights to its design and drawings?
o: The intellectual property for the design is still the architect's because it only becomes the owner's AFTER the project is built
The intellectual property for the design is the owner's until the project is built
The intellectual property for the design remains the same because the construction of the project is irrelevant to intellectual property
The intellectual property for the design does not exist until the project is built
n: Copyright over the design stays with the architect whether or not the project is built.

q: Which of these business structures must be registered with the SEC?
n: Partnerships and corporations register with the SEC; sole proprietorships register with the DTI.

q: For small-scale projects, which method of architect selection is advised?
o: All of the above are recommended
n: Direct selection suits small projects; competitions and comparative selection are for larger or public ones.

q: In an architectural design competition, which statement about the jury is correct?
o: There should be at least seven members
All of the jurors must be licensed architects because only then will they be qualified to judge the designs
n: A jury is odd-numbered, usually five, and need not be all architects, so none of the statements holds.

q: Under the rules for architectural design competitions, how many jury seats may the project owner's representatives occupy?
o: The owner is not entitled to place any representative on the jury
The owner may designate only a single representative
The owner may name as many representatives as desired, so long as they remain fewer than half the panel
The owner may designate up to two representatives
n: The owner may seat one representative; the rest of the jury are independent professionals.

q: Which term describes the in-depth study, built on earlier pre-feasibility work and primary data collection, that establishes whether a proposed development is viable?
o: Site utilization and land use studies
n: A feasibility study builds on the pre-feasibility study with primary data to decide whether the project is viable.

q: SPP 201 defines a process whose objective is to deliver the full project program without cost overruns. What is this process called?
n: Value management aims to deliver the full program within budget; value engineering reviews specific items for savings.

q: According to SPP 201, which manner of delivering predesign services is disallowed?
o: SPP 201 places no restriction on any of these delivery methods
n: Pre-design services may be done alone, through the architect's staff or with other firms.

q: Under the multiple-of-direct-personnel-expense compensation method, which item is added on top of the computed Fee to arrive at the client's total billing?
n: Reimbursable expenses are billed on top of the fee computed as a multiple of direct personnel expense.

q: For an ongoing client relationship spanning multiple successive projects, which compensation arrangement does the SPP recommend?
n: For a continuing series of projects, a professional fee plus expenses is recommended.

q: When a client asks an architect to devote personal time to work outside the normal scope, which charges may properly apply?
o: All of these may be charged
n: Personal time outside the scope may be billed as per diem, honorarium or reimbursable expenses.

q: Among the phases of an architect's regular design services, which one is NOT actually included?
n: Regular design services run from project definition through schematic design, design development, contract documents, bidding and construction; site development is not a phase.

q: Which task falls outside an architect's scope of work under regular design services?
o: Making periodic visits to the construction site
n: Building maintenance is a post-construction service, outside regular design services.

q: When acting as construction manager, which of these does NOT belong among the architect's responsibilities?
n: A construction manager controls cost, time and quality and keeps records but does not redesign.

q: What term names the systematic layout of a parcel of land for both the vertical structures (buildings, monuments) and horizontal features (RROWs) to be built on it?
n: Physical planning lays out a parcel for buildings (vertical) and roads (horizontal).

q: Under the SPP classification of services, forensic architecture falls under which category?
n: Forensic architecture is one of the specialized architectural services.

q: Construction Management services are governed by which numbered SPP document?
n: SPP 204A covers full-time supervision and SPP 204B construction management.

q: Your friend, a registered landscape architect, lives in your condominium and collects association dues from residents. What category of service is this an example of?
n: Managing a property after completion, such as collecting dues, is a post-construction service.

q: Your boss proposed handling every stage of a project for the client, from predesign through post-construction, under a single engagement, sparing the client from juggling multiple contracts. What kind of service did your boss offer?
n: Comprehensive architectural services bundle pre-design through post-construction under one engagement.

q: What range of multiplier does the SPP recommend for the multiple-of-direct-personnel-expense method of compensation?
n: The SPP multiplier for direct personnel expense is 1.5 to 2.5 to cover overhead and profit.

q: At which stage(s) of regular design services must the architect submit or update the SPPCC?
n: The architect submits the Statement of Probable Project Construction Cost at schematic design and updates it at design development and contract documents.

q: Under SPP 202's project-complexity classification, which building type belongs to Group 2?
n: Shopping malls are Group 2 (moderately complex); printing plants are Group 1 and auditoriums Group 3.

q: In SPP 202's complexity classification, which of these facility types are Group 3?
n: Airports, aquariums and gymnasiums are all Group 3 exceptional-complexity facilities.

q: SPP 202 places projects whose plans and contract documents are reused unchanged for repetitive, similar buildings into which classification group?
n: Reuse of the same plans for repetitive buildings is Group 6, billed at reduced rates.

q: Once the architect has finished preparing all contract documents, what percentage of his Detailed Design and Contract Documents Phase work is deemed complete?
n: Finishing the contract documents counts as 90% of that phase; the rest comes with bidding assistance.

q: If construction work is suspended for eight months, what happens to the architect's fee covering the remaining, not-yet-performed works?
o: It is withheld by the owner until completion of the project.
It is withheld by the owner until the issues on-site are resolved.
n: If work is suspended for more than six months, the fee for the unperformed work is doubled.

q: How is the architect's professional fee characterized in relation to deductions and taxes?
o: Immune to all forms of taxes
Both a net amount and immune to taxes
n: The fee is a net amount: taxes and deductions are added, not taken out of it.

q: Which cost item is excluded from the PCC?
o: None of these belong in the PCC
n: Project construction cost excludes the land; the land belongs to the project development cost.

q: Among these cost figures associated with a project, which is typically the biggest?
o: PCC and PDC, tied for largest
n: Project development cost (PDC) includes land, construction and all fees, so it is the largest figure.

q: Which planning service concentrates on the non-physical and non-engineering aspects of a master development plan?
n: Comprehensive development planning covers the non-physical, non-engineering side: socio-economic and institutional plans.

q: On the project team, who is tasked with planning, programming and monitoring the various activities, while acting as an adviser on material costs and construction methods?
n: The project manager plans, programs and monitors activities and advises on costs and methods.

q: May an architect who renders design-build services offer the client a guaranteed maximum construction cost?
o: Yes, because this is one of the SPP-recognized ways of rendering design-build services
No, because estimates should never be guaranteed by the architect
No, because the architect is not allowed to build his own project and must hire a third party contractor
Both of the preceding reasons apply
n: Design-build services may carry a guaranteed maximum cost, one of the SPP-recognized arrangements.

q: For purposes of obtaining the FSCCR, who shall certify that all fire protection and life safety features indicated in the FSCR for Building Permit, including approved amendments, have been properly installed and implemented?
n: For the FSCCR, the contractor certifies that the fire and life safety features were installed as approved.

q: For purposes of obtaining the FSCR, who shall ensure and certify that the design, criteria and specifications of all fire safety features are appropriate to the proposed project and compliant with RA 9514?
n: For the FSCR, the architect certifies that the fire safety design meets RA 9514.

q: Per RA 9514, what tread depth must newly constructed stairs meet at minimum?
n: New stairs need treads of at least 280 mm and risers of 100 to 180 mm.

q: RA 9514 sets what minimum riser height for new stairs?
n: New stair risers must be at least 100 mm and at most 180 mm.

q: Which handrail height complies with the Fire Code (RA 9514 RIRR)?
n: Stair handrails must be 865 to 965 mm above the tread nosing; only 870 mm falls in that range.

q: For occupant-load purposes under RA 9514, how much floor area must be allotted per person in the sleeping departments of hospitals?
n: Hospital sleeping departments use 11.1 sqm per person; treatment areas use 22.3 sqm.

q: RA 9514 requires how much floor area per person for a store's basement-level back-of-house office space?
n: Business uses, including back offices, use 9.3 sqm per person.

q: Under RA 9514, how many exits are required if the occupant load is 600?
n: An occupant load of 500 to 1,000 needs at least 3 exits.

q: What minimum frontage must a socialized duplex housing lot provide?
n: Socialized duplex lots need a 6 m frontage.

q: For existing stairs, RA 9514 sets the minimum tread at:
n: Existing stairs may keep treads down to 230 mm.

q: RA 9514 requires ramps to be at least how wide?
n: Ramps in a means of egress must be at least 1,120 mm wide.

q: According to the NBC, how deep must an elevator pit be at minimum?
n: Elevator pits must be at least 600 mm deep below the car.
ref: IRR of PD 1096, Rule XII — elevators

q: For standing-room areas in places of assembly, the NBC allots how much area per person?
n: Standing room in assembly places is figured at 0.28 sqm per person; general assembly at 0.65 sqm.
ref: IRR of PD 1096, Rule XII — occupant loads

q: How far must a firewall extend under the eaves, according to the NBC?
n: Firewalls must extend 300 mm under the eaves as well as above the roof.

q: What minimum floor area does the NBC require for a single-occupancy condominium unit in a medium-cost development?
n: Single-occupancy condominium units need at least 18 sqm (12 sqm net may be allowed).

q: BP 220 sets the minimum width of a pathwalk at:
n: BP 220 pathwalks are 3.0 m wide; alleys are 2.0 m.

q: What is the minimum passageway width required for courts, according to the NBC?
n: Courts need a passageway at least 1.20 m wide for access and cleaning.

q: Per BP 344, how far from a dead end may the required turning space be located, at most?
n: Turnabout spaces must be within 3.50 m of every dead end.

q: Under the 1994 IRR of BP 344, what was the maximum mounting height of a flush control in an accessible toilet?
n: The 1994 IRR capped flush controls at 1.20 m; the 2024 IRR instead requires tank-type water closets with lever flush valves.

q: For an occupant load greater than 10, the NBC requires stairs at least how wide?
n: Stairs for more than 10 occupants need 0.90 m; above 50 occupants need 1.10 m.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, how deep must the warning tactile blocks at the start and end of a staircase be?
n: Warning tactile blocks 600 mm deep are set 300 mm from the start and end of the stairs across the full width. The 1994 IRR used a 300 mm strip.

q: What is the steepest longitudinal slope BP 344 allows for a walkway?
n: Walkways should be no steeper than 1:20 along their length.

q: BP 344 limits a walkway's cross (side-to-side) gradient to no steeper than:
n: Walkways may have a cross gradient of at most 1:100 (1%).

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, how must gratings on a walkway be installed?
o: Up to 6.5 mm above the floor
Up to 13 mm above the floor
n: Gratings must be level with the floor, slip-resistant and with openings no wider than 13 mm. The 1994 IRR allowed a 6.5 mm projection.

q: For a handrail mounted vertically on top of a ledge, BP 344 requires what minimum clearance?
n: Handrails on ledges need 40 mm clearance; on walls 50 mm.

q: What minimum clearance does BP 344 require for a handrail mounted horizontally onto a wall?
n: Wall-mounted handrails need 50 mm clear from the wall.

q: BP 344 assumes a maximum pedestrian crossing speed of:
n: Crossing times are set for a walking speed of 0.9 m/s, not the usual 1.2 m/s.

q: A single floor has 24 water closet stalls for women and 18 water closet stalls for men. How many accessible toilet stalls need to be provided for that entire floor?
n: One accessible cubicle per sex for every 20 or fewer cubicles: 24 women's stalls need 2, 18 men's need 1, so 3 in all.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, which doorknob mounting height complies?
n: Sec. C.2.11: door handles and lever locksets are centered 900 mm above the floor. The old 0.82-1.06 m range from the 1994 IRR no longer applies.

q: How far must the ingress point of a traffic generating building be from a major road intersection, at minimum?
n: Entrances of traffic-generating buildings must be at least 50 m from a major intersection.

q: The NBC sets the minimum foundation thickness for Group A dwellings at:
n: Footings for Group A dwellings must be at least 250 mm thick.

q: For pedestrian protection, what minimum vertical clearance must be kept between the top of the sidewalk and the lowest part of the street canopy?
n: Pedestrian canopies must clear the sidewalk by at least 2.40 m.

q: The NBC requires a single-loaded aisle to be at least how wide?
n: Aisles serving seats on one side must be at least 800 mm wide; on both sides 1.20 m.

q: Which of these does NOT require a wet standpipe, according to the NBC?
o: Group C occupancy 2 or more storeys in height
Group H or I occupancy of any height
Group H buildings without stage whose seating capacity is less than 500
Groups B, D, E, F and G 3 or more storeys in height
n: Assembly buildings without a stage and under 500 seats need no wet standpipe.

q: What is the steepest angle of inclination the NBC allows for an escalator?
n: Escalators may not be inclined more than 30° from the horizontal.

q: A condominium project has 12 condo units and is 900 meters away from the nearest public park. How much space should be allotted to parks and playgrounds inside the condo development?
n: Condominium parks are figured per unit when no public park lies within reach, here 56 sqm for 12 units.

q: BP 220 requires a dwelling's main door to be at least how wide?
n: BP 220 main doors are at least 0.80 m wide; bathroom doors 0.60 m.

q: Under the NBC, what is the minimum rear setback for R1?
n: R-1 rear setbacks are at least 2.00 m.

q: What is the minimum window area the NBC requires for a habitable room?
o: 5% of floor area but not less than 240sqmm
10% of floor area but not less than 1sqm
5% of floor area but not less than 1sqm
10% of floor area but not less than 240sqmm
n: Windows must equal 10% of the floor area and never less than 1.00 sqm.

q: What is the name of the approved security a contractor and his surety furnish to guarantee good-faith execution of the work in accordance with the contract terms?
n: A performance bond guarantees the contractor will carry out the work as contracted.

q: What term names the approved security posted by a contractor and his surety, guaranteeing good faith on the part of the contractor to pay all obligations arising from the contract?
n: A payment bond guarantees the contractor will pay labor, suppliers and other obligations.

q: What bond guarantees the quality of the materials, equipment and workmanship the contractor delivers?
n: A guarantee (warranty) bond covers quality after completion; a performance bond covers faithful execution, and a payment bond covers the contractor's bills.

q: What is the person, firm or corporation that guarantees the contractor's bonds called?
n: The surety stands behind the contractor (the principal) and pays the owner (the obligee) if the contractor defaults.

q: What term refers to the printed documents stipulating the procedural and administrative aspects of the contract?
n: General conditions set the procedural and administrative rules of the contract.

q: Which contract term shall be understood to mean “purchase and/or fabricate and deliver to the jobsite or other location when so designated”?
n: Furnish means purchase or fabricate and deliver to the site.

q: Which contract term shall mean to build in, mount in position, connect or apply any object specified ready for the intended use?
n: Install means build in, mount, connect or apply ready for use.

q: Which single contract term shall be understood to mean “furnish and install”?
n: Provide means furnish and install.

q: At what point is the work considered “substantially completed”?
o: When the amount of completed work is equal to 95% or more of the contract amount
Only after the Period of Making Good of Known Defects or Faults
When the amount of completed work is equal to 98% or more of the contract amount
When the amount of completed work is equal to 97% or more of the contract amount
n: The work is taken as substantially complete once accomplished work reaches 98% of the contract amount.

q: The Period of Making Good of Known Defects or Faults usually lasts for 60 days maximum, unless otherwise stated in the contract. From what point does this period begin to run?
o: Three months after the date of the final payment
When the Certificate of Completion is issued
When the contractor receives the Notice to Proceed
When the work completed is equivalent to at least 95% of the contract amount
n: The period for correcting known defects runs from the issue of the Certificate of Completion.

q: Absent any agreement to the contrary, who shall shoulder the costs for permits and licenses needed for the project, according to UAP Doc. 301?
n: Unless the contract says otherwise, the contractor pays for permits and licenses.

q: Establishing the boundary lines of the property is whose responsibility?
n: The owner furnishes the survey and establishes the property boundaries.

q: If there is a conflict between the specs and the drawings, which should be followed?
n: Where specifications and drawings conflict, the specifications govern.

q: Which of these are part of the contract documents?
n: General conditions, special provisions and specifications are all contract documents.

q: What is the minimum ceiling height for a one-storey artificially ventilated structure, according to the NBC?
n: A one-storey building with artificial ventilation needs 2.40 m ceilings.

q: For places of assembly generally, according to the NBC, how much area per person is required?
n: Assembly areas with fixed seating are figured at 0.65 sqm per person; standing room 0.28 sqm.

q: What is the maximum length of dead ends, according to the NBC?
n: Dead-end corridors may not exceed 6.00 m.

q: What is the term for an architect registered and licensed or permitted to practice under RA 9266 who is professionally and academically qualified, with exceptional or recognized expertise or specialization in any branch of architecture?
n: A consulting architect is an RLA with recognized expertise in a branch of architecture.

q: Per the IRR of RA 9266, which business form is treated as synonymous with an "architectural company"?
n: The IRR treats an architectural company as a partnership.

q: What is the term for the proprietary rights retained by an architect over any architectural work that he prepares, including the right to control the erection of any building which reproduces his design whether in whole or in part?
n: Copyright lets the architect control any reproduction of the design, in whole or in part.

q: During construction, an architect issues an additional drawing that adds cost beyond the original design. May the contractor pass that extra cost on to the owner?
o: No. The contract is fixed and cannot be changed, so the contractor needs to follow the original design.
No. The cost must be charged to the architect because it is he who issued the drawings and the changes contained in the drawing.
Yes, but the owner has the right to charge the cost to the architect because the owner did not order the change.
Yes, as long as he gives written notice to the architect regarding the extra cost within 15 days of receiving the instruction.
n: Extra work from added drawings may be charged if the contractor gives the architect written notice within 15 days.

q: What is the term for the proprietary rights to an architectural work held by a person who commissions the architect for the said work, limited to use of the design for one project only?
n: The commissioning owner gets ownership of the design for one project only; copyright stays with the architect.

q: Which is NOT actually a document that needs to be submitted when applying to take the licensure examination for architects?
o: Certificate of Live Birth in National Statistics Office (NSO) Security Paper
Marriage Contract in NSO Security Paper for married male applicants
n: Marriage contracts are needed only by married female applicants whose surname changed.

q: Who decides on the design of the architect's seal?
o: The architect is free to choose his own seal design
n: The PRBOA (PRBArch) prescribes the design of the seal.

q: The provision of RA 9266 regarding the ownership of plans, specifications, and other contract documents needs to be incorporated by all architects in all contract documents and other instruments of service. Which provision is this?
n: Section 33 covers ownership of plans and must appear in all instruments of service.

q: What happens when the architect is only able to condemn inferior work a month before substantial completion?
o: The contractor still needs to rectify it because it is inferior work, at no cost to the owner.
The contractor will rectify the inferior work but will charge the cost of rectification to the owner because the condemnation period expires no later than 6 months from substantial completion.

Since the condemnation period has already expired, the owner may cross charge to the architect the cost for rectification. This may be deducted from the architect's remaining fee for construction supervision.
n: Inferior work must be corrected at no cost to the owner whenever it is condemned before acceptance.

q: For a corporation to be registered for the corporate practice of architecture, at least what fraction of the owners, shareholders, members, etc. of that firm must be RLAs?
n: At least 75% of the owners, shareholders or members must be registered architects.

q: Vacant seats on the PRBArch are filled based on nominations from whom?
o: Any RLA is entitled to make nominations for the vacancy
n: Vacancies are filled from nominees of the IAPOA, which is the UAP.

q: When a foreign national partners with a Filipino counterpart to render architectural services in the Philippines, which of the two is designated architect of record?
n: The Filipino counterpart is the architect of record; the foreign architect only consults.

q: Per UAP Document 301, whose job is it to arrange water, power, and telephone connections with the utility companies for the jobsite?
n: The contractor arranges temporary water, power and telephone connections.

q: Should one section of the IRR of RA 9266 be struck down as unconstitutional, what is the effect on its remaining sections?
o: They shall be invalidated as well
They need to be passed into law again in order to take effect
Their validity will be cast in doubt
n: The separability clause keeps the other sections in force.

q: Which statement about the IAPOA is NOT true?
o: The UAP is the current IAPOA
The IAPOA must be a non-profit, non-stock corporation
All registered architects automatically become members of the IAPOA
The IAPOA must be registered with the DTI and the PRBOA
n: The IAPOA is registered with the SEC as a non-stock, non-profit corporation, not with the DTI.

q: To pass the licensure board exam, what minimum average score must a candidate achieve?
n: Passing requires a 70% general average with no grade below 50%.
